title: The Shortest War in History Lasted 38 Minutes
description:
On August 27, 1896, Britain went to war with Zanzibar. The shooting started at 9:02 in the morning and stopped around 9:40: the shortest war on record.
🚶 Visiting San Diego? Explore its history on a guided tour with Fable: https://fablehospitality.com

Every frame is drawn with code. No stock footage, no AI video.

0:00 The shortest war in history
0:06 Zanzibar, 1896
0:11 Sultan Hamad bin Thuwaini dies
0:16 Khalid bin Barghash takes the palace
0:21 Britain's warships
0:25 2,800 men behind the barricades
0:29 The ultimatum: 9 a.m., August 27
0:35 Nine o'clock
0:37 9:02: the bombardment begins
0:40 The Glasgow is sunk
0:45 9:40: the palace burns, the flag comes down
0:50 About 500 vs. one
0:55 Khalid flees; a new sultan
1:00 The bill for the shells
1:04 38 minutes

Note: sources give 38, 40 or 45 minutes, depending on whether the war starts at the 9:00 order or the 9:02 first shot and ends at 9:40 or 9:45. Casualty figures (about 500 killed or wounded on the Zanzibari side) are estimates.

Images (public domain, The Illustrated London News, Sept. 5, 1896, via the Internet Archive): "The Crisis at Zanzibar: British War-Ships Engaged in the Bombardment of the Sultan's Palace" (Fred T. Jane); Hamad bin Thuwaini, the late Sultan; panoramic view of Zanzibar; Palace Square, Zanzibar; the "Glasgow", the Zanzibar gun-boat sunk by the British. The palace harem after the bombardment, 1896 (Richard Dorsey Mohun, public domain, Wikimedia Commons).
Maps drawn in code from Natural Earth (world-atlas) outlines.
Facts: Anglo-Zanzibar War (27 August 1896) as summarized from period reporting (Illustrated London News, Sept. 5, 1896) and modern histories; the 300,000-rupee payment covered the shells fired and looting damage.
Narration voice is synthetic.
